position: before its word — or end, after a verb (*rest a bit*)
contrast: Before a plain adjective it prefers unwelcome qualities: *a bit late*, *a bit tired*, not *a bit wonderful* — use *a little* or *pretty* there. Before a noun it needs *of*: *a bit of luck*.

senses.gloss: To a small degree; slightly, or for a short time.
examples: I'm *a bit* worried about the weather.
Could you turn the music down *a bit*?
Let's wait *a bit* before we call him.

contrast: Also an adjective before a noun (*an a cappella group*). Spelled with two *p*'s and two *l*'s.

senses.gloss: With voices only, without instruments.
examples: The choir sang the last hymn *a cappella*.
When the sound system failed, she finished the song *a cappella*.
The group records all its music *a cappella*.

position: before its word — before a comparative (*a good deal better*); end after a verb
contrast: Not the noun *a good deal* (выгодная сделка): *I got a good deal on the car*. Before a noun it needs *of*: *a good deal of time*.

senses.gloss: Much; considerably, with a comparative or *too*.
examples: She looks *a good deal* better than she did last week.
The new route is *a good deal* shorter.

senses.gloss: A lot; much or often, with a verb.
examples: He travels *a good deal* for work.
We've talked about it *a good deal* at home.

position: before its word — before a comparative (*a great deal easier*); end after a verb
contrast: More formal than *a lot*, and the natural choice in affirmative sentences where *much* sounds stiff: *He worries a great deal*, not *He worries much*.

senses.gloss: Much; far, with a comparative or *too*.
examples: Things are *a great deal* easier now.
The repair cost *a great deal* more than we expected.

senses.gloss: Very much or very often, with a verb.
examples: She has traveled *a great deal* since she retired.
I've thought about your offer *a great deal*.

modifies: verbs of ordering, buying and pricing
form: French *à la carte*, 'by the menu'; usually written without the accent in American English
contrast: Also an adjective (*an a la carte menu*). It has spread from restaurants to anything sold item by item.

senses.gloss: Ordered or priced item by item, not as part of a set meal or package.
examples: We skipped the buffet and ordered *a la carte*.
Side dishes are sold *a la carte*.
The app lets you buy extra features *a la carte*.

position: before its word — or end, after a verb (*relax a little*)
contrast: *A little* is positive (немного); *little* without *a* is negative (мало): *He sleeps a little in the afternoon* vs *He sleeps little*. Unlike *a bit*, it sits comfortably before pleasant adjectives: *a little happier*.

senses.gloss: To a small degree; slightly.
examples: I'm *a little* tired after the flight.
Could you speak *a little* louder?
Let's rest *a little* before we go on.

position: end — after the verb and object; before its word with a comparative (*a lot better*)
contrast: Always two words: *alot* is a misspelling. It cannot go before a plain adjective: *a lot better*, but not *a lot good* — say *very good*. Informal; in formal writing prefer *much* or *a great deal*.

senses.gloss: Much; far, with a comparative.
examples: I feel *a lot* better today.
This phone is *a lot* cheaper online.

senses.gloss: Very much or very often, with a verb.
examples: We go to the beach *a lot* in the summer.
Thanks *a lot* for your help.
He talks *a lot* when he's nervous.

contrast: Mostly written; in speech Americans say *a little* or *a bit*. The noun *trifle* means a small unimportant thing.

senses.gloss: Slightly; a little.
examples: She seemed *a trifle* annoyed by the question.
The soup was *a trifle* too salty.
He arrived *a trifle* late, as usual.

type: focusing — marks the most important item
position: front or end — often front with a comma, or right before the item it stresses
modifies: a whole clause, or the phrase it singles out
contrast: Not *first of all*: *first of all* orders points (во-первых), *above all* ranks them (самое главное).

senses.gloss: Most importantly; more than anything else.
examples: *Above all*, don't panic.
She wanted, *above all*, to be taken seriously.
Be kind, be honest, and *above all*, be yourself.

type: manner — applying equally to every member of a group
modifies: verbs of cutting, raising and applying
contrast: Also an adjective with hyphens before a noun: *an across-the-board tax cut*.

senses.gloss: Equally for everyone or everything in a group; without exception.
senses.ru: для всех без исключения, по всем направлениям
examples: The company cut salaries *across the board*.
Prices rose *across the board* last month.
The new rules apply *across the board*.

modifies: verbs of going on and repeating; the end of a list

senses.gloss: Forever; again and again without end.
examples: The list of complaints could go on *ad infinitum*.
We can't keep extending the deadline *ad infinitum*.
The pattern repeats *ad infinitum*.

type: frequency — so often that it becomes tiresome
modifies: verbs of repeating, discussing and playing

senses.gloss: Repeated so often or so long that people are sick of it.
examples: The ad played *ad nauseam* during the game.
They discussed the budget *ad nauseam*.
He quotes that movie *ad nauseam*.

type: degree — a downtoner: not well, but somewhat
contrast: Nothing to do with fashion as clothing: *She can sew, after a fashion* means she sews, but not well.

senses.gloss: In a rough or imperfect way; to some extent.
examples: I speak Spanish, *after a fashion*.
The repair worked, *after a fashion*.
He apologized, *after a fashion*.

position: front or end — end when it means *despite what was expected*, usually front when it gives a reason
contrast: Not *после всего*, and not *finally*: for the last step in a sequence use *finally* or *in the end*. Position carries the meaning: *He came after all* (всё-таки пришёл) vs *After all, he's your brother* (он ведь твой брат).

senses.gloss: In spite of what was expected or planned.
examples: It didn't rain *after all*.
So you decided to come *after all*!
The test wasn't that hard *after all*.

senses.gloss: Used to give a reason that should be kept in mind.
examples: Don't be so hard on him. *After all*, he's only six.
We should invite her; she is, *after all*, part of the team.

contrast: Also an adjective with a hyphen: *an after-hours club*.

senses.gloss: After the normal working or opening hours.
examples: The staff often stay *after hours* to finish orders.
The building is locked *after hours*.
I don't answer work email *after hours*.

ru: снова и снова, раз за разом

senses.gloss: Many times; repeatedly.
examples: I've told you *again and again* to lock the door.
She watched the video *again and again*.
The same problem comes up *again and again*.

type: manner — in a hurry to meet a deadline

senses.gloss: As fast as possible, to finish before a deadline.
examples: Rescue teams are working *against the clock* to reach the miners.
We were racing *against the clock* to finish the report.
In the final round, contestants cook *against the clock*.

type: manner — in a position of advantage

senses.gloss: In a strong position, having prepared earlier than others or than needed.
examples: If you start saving now, you'll be *ahead of the game*.
She reads industry reports to stay *ahead of the game*.
We filed our taxes in February, so we're *ahead of the game*.

contrast: Everyday American for *in advance*. Compare *on time* (вовремя) and *in time* (успеть к сроку).

senses.gloss: Before the time something happens or is due; in advance.
examples: Call *ahead of time* to reserve a table.
I cook most of the meal *ahead of time*.
The train arrived ten minutes *ahead of time*.

ru: всё это время, с самого начала
contrast: With a following noun it is a preposition about space: *trees all along the river*. The adverb means the whole time, often with the sense that someone knew or was right: *I knew it all along*.

senses.gloss: The whole time; from the very beginning.
senses.ru: всё это время, с самого начала
examples: I knew *all along* that he was lying.
The keys were in my pocket *all along*.
She was right *all along*.

senses.gloss: Suddenly; without warning.
examples: *All at once*, the lights went out.
*All at once* she started to cry.

senses.gloss: All together at the same time.
examples: Don't eat the candy *all at once*.
Everyone started talking *all at once*.

ru: в общем и целом, в целом

senses.gloss: Considering everything; on the whole.
examples: *All in all*, it was a good year.
There were a few problems, but *all in all* the trip went well.
*All in all*, I'd recommend the hotel.

contrast: More informal and more dramatic than *suddenly*. Many Americans say *all of the sudden*, but it is marked wrong in writing.

senses.gloss: Suddenly and unexpectedly.
examples: *All of a sudden*, the dog started barking.
I felt dizzy *all of a sudden*.
Why are you so interested in cooking *all of a sudden*?

contrast: With a following noun it is a preposition: *all over the world*. *It's all over* (всё кончено) is an adjective use meaning *finished*.

senses.gloss: Everywhere; in every part of a place.
examples: I've looked *all over* for my glasses.
There was broken glass *all over*.

senses.gloss: Over the whole body or surface.
examples: I ache *all over* after that workout.
She was shaking *all over*.

modifies: verbs; or a whole statement, placed after it
contrast: *Alright* is common in informal writing but still marked wrong in formal American English. *I'm all right* (в порядке) and *Is it all right if…?* (можно ли) are adjective uses, and *All right, let's go* is an interjection.

senses.gloss: Well enough; satisfactorily.
examples: The interview went *all right*, I think.
Are you getting along *all right* at the new job?
The old laptop still works *all right*.

senses.gloss: Certainly; without any doubt, after a statement.
examples: That's him *all right* — I'd know that laugh anywhere.
She was angry *all right*.

position: front or end — front with a comma, or at the end of the clause
contrast: *It's all the same to me* (мне всё равно) is a different, adjective use meaning *it makes no difference*.

senses.gloss: In spite of that; nevertheless.
examples: He's annoying, but I like him *all the same*.
*All the same*, you should have called.
I don't need a ride, but thanks *all the same*.

senses.gloss: Very often; constantly.
examples: She complains *all the time*.
This kind of thing happens *all the time* in big cities.
We eat at that diner *all the time*.

senses.gloss: During the whole of a period, often without someone knowing.
examples: I searched everywhere, and the ticket was in my wallet *all the time*.
He was listening *all the time* we were talking.

modifies: verbs of movement; verbs of turning, reading and supporting

senses.gloss: For the whole distance.
examples: We walked *all the way* home.
She drove *all the way* from Chicago.

senses.gloss: Completely; to the end.
examples: Turn the volume *all the way* down.
I'm with you *all the way*.
Read the contract *all the way* through before you sign.

contrast: Not *altogether* (совсем; в целом): *We sang all together* vs *I'm not altogether sure*. Test: if you can split it — *We all sang together* — write two words.

senses.gloss: As a group, in one place or at the same time.
examples: Let's sing it *all together* from the top.
Put the receipts *all together* in one folder.
It's nice to have the family *all together* for once.

modifies: a whole clause, usually one with a number

senses.gloss: Counting everyone or everything; in all.
examples: *All told*, the repairs cost $4,000.
There were about fifty guests *all told*.
*All told*, we spent three weeks on the road.

type: degree — an intensifier with a regretful tone
modifies: adjectives and adverbs (*all too often*, *all too soon*)

senses.gloss: Much more than is good or wanted; far too.
examples: The vacation ended *all too* soon.
Mistakes like this are *all too* common.
I know that feeling *all too* well.

position: end — after the last item of a list
contrast: A little more formal than *and so on*; the two are interchangeable. Do not add *etc.* after either.

senses.gloss: And other similar things; and the rest.
examples: Bring towels, sunscreen, snacks, *and so forth*.
We talked about jobs, housing, *and so forth*.
The form asks for your name, address, *and so forth*.

position: end — after the last item of a list
contrast: The everyday form; *and so on and so forth* is an emphatic spoken version.

senses.gloss: And other things of the same kind; and the rest.
examples: She teaches math, physics, chemistry, *and so on*.
You still have rent, bills, taxes, *and so on*.
First one person complained, then another, *and so on*.

type: degree — even more than was said
modifies: a statement of amount or quality

senses.gloss: And even more than that.
examples: He paid back the loan *and then some*.
The new model does everything the old one did, *and then some*.
The renovation will cost fifty thousand dollars *and then some*.

contrast: Used with *not* or in questions: *She doesn't live here any longer*. The more formal *no longer* goes mid-sentence: *She no longer lives here*. Russian *больше не* is not *not more*.

senses.gloss: From now or from then on; anymore.
examples: I can't wait *any longer*.
He doesn't work here *any longer*.
Nobody uses these phones *any longer*.

contrast: Also an adjective with hyphens: *around-the-clock care*. British English also says *round the clock*.

senses.gloss: All day and all night, without stopping.
examples: Doctors worked *around the clock* during the outbreak.
The store is open *around the clock*.
Crews are clearing snow *around the clock*.

type: stance — adds a surprising or correcting fact
contrast: Close to *actually* and *in fact*. Russian *фактически* is closer to *in effect* or *practically*.

senses.gloss: In fact; actually, especially when adding something surprising.
examples: *As a matter of fact*, I've never been to New York.
I'm not tired. *As a matter of fact*, I feel great.
We've met before, *as a matter of fact*.

modifies: *be* and verbs of stating, listing or doing
contrast: Always *follows*, even before a list of many items: *The rules are as follows*, never *as follow*.

senses.gloss: In the way described next.
examples: The winners are *as follows*: Smith, Garcia and Lee.
The recipe goes *as follows*.
Proceed *as follows*: open the lid, remove the filter, and rinse it.

ru: и так уже; а на деле
contrast: The literal use means *in its present form*: *Leave the room as it is* (как есть). The idiom points to the real situation, often worse than hoped.

senses.gloss: Already, even without anything more being added.
examples: Don't order more food — we have too much *as it is*.
I'm late *as it is*; I can't stop for coffee.

senses.gloss: In reality, as things actually are, in contrast to what was hoped.
examples: We hoped to finish by May. *As it is*, we'll be lucky to finish by August.
I wanted to lend him money; *as it is*, I can barely pay my own bills.

type: stance — softens an unusual word or image
position: end — or mid, right after the phrase it softens
modifies: a word or phrase used loosely
contrast: A fixed form: never *as it was*. Slightly formal; it flags a metaphor, like Russian *так сказать*.

senses.gloss: So to speak; shows that a word is not meant literally.
examples: He became, *as it were*, a stranger in his own home.
She's the face of the company, *as it were*.
We're all in the same boat, *as it were*.

type: stance — comments on luck, good or bad
contrast: It can go either way; the context decides between *к счастью* and *как назло*.

senses.gloss: By chance, whether fortunate or unfortunate.
examples: *As luck would have it*, a taxi was passing just then.
*As luck would have it*, it rained on the only day we went to the beach.
*As luck would have it*, my old roommate was the hiring manager.

type: focusing — the thing itself, in the strict sense
contrast: Careful writers use it only to point back to a noun: *He's a guest, and as such he should be treated well*. Many Americans now use *As such,* to mean *therefore*; editors often mark that wrong.

senses.gloss: In the exact sense of the word; strictly speaking.
examples: There's no fee *as such*, but you pay for materials.
I'm not a chef *as such*, but I love to cook.

senses.gloss: In that role or capacity.
examples: She is the team leader, and *as such* she makes the final call.
The house is a landmark and is protected *as such*.

type: place — measured in a straight line

senses.gloss: In a straight line, not following roads.
examples: The town is ten miles away *as the crow flies*, but twenty by car.
*As the crow flies*, we live close to the airport.
It's only a mile *as the crow flies*.

type: manner — the way things usually happen
contrast: Always *as usual*, never *as usually*.

senses.gloss: In the way that usually happens.
examples: *As usual*, he was late.
The store opened at nine *as usual*.
She ordered the pasta, *as usual*.

contrast: *As well* goes at the end: *I speak French as well*. *As well as* (а также) links to a noun: *I speak French as well as Spanish*. *Might as well* means there is no reason not to: *We might as well go home*.

senses.gloss: Also; too.
examples: Can I get fries *as well*?
She's a singer, and she writes songs *as well*.
If you're going, I'll come *as well*.

position: mid or end — mid after the auxiliary (*has as yet*), or end
modifies: verbs, usually negative; *un-* adjectives (*as yet unknown*)
contrast: More formal than *yet* or *so far*.

senses.gloss: Until now; so far.
examples: The cause of the fire is *as yet* unknown.
No one has *as yet* claimed responsibility.
We have received no reply *as yet*.

modifies: verbs of selling, running and operating
contrast: After *be*, *at a loss* usually means puzzled: *I'm at a loss for words* (не знаю, что сказать) — an adjective use. The business opposite is *at a profit*.

senses.gloss: For less money than it cost.
examples: They had to sell the house *at a loss*.
The store has been operating *at a loss* for two years.
Airlines often fly these routes *at a loss*.

position: end — after a number (*one at a time*)
contrast: *At a time* counts things together: *two at a time* (по двое). *At one time* means *formerly*, and *at times* means *sometimes*.

senses.gloss: Together in one group, or in one stretch without stopping.
examples: Please come in one *at a time*.
He ran up the stairs two steps *at a time*.
She sometimes works for twelve hours *at a time*.

type: degree — strengthens a negative or question
position: end — or right after the negative word (*not at all*)
contrast: Only with negatives, questions and *if*: *I don't like it at all*, never *I like it at all*. *Not at all* is also a polite reply to thanks.

senses.gloss: In any way; to any degree.
examples: I didn't sleep *at all* last night.
Do you speak any Russian *at all*?
If you have any questions *at all*, just call.

contrast: Always plural *costs* in this form; the singular version is *at any cost*.

senses.gloss: Whatever it takes; no matter what the price or sacrifice.
examples: The general wanted to win *at all costs*.
Avoid that highway *at all costs* during rush hour.
The secret must be kept *at all costs*.

ru: во всяком случае; по крайней мере

senses.gloss: Anyway; used to move on or return to the main point.
senses.ru: во всяком случае, так или иначе
examples: I'm not sure who won. *At any rate*, it's over.
*At any rate*, we should get going.

senses.gloss: At least; used to correct or limit what was just said.
examples: He's a good teacher — *at any rate*, the students like him.
It was a success, or *at any rate* not a disaster.

type: manner — at a distance, not letting someone close
contrast: In business, *an arm's-length deal* is one between independent parties with no special relationship.

senses.gloss: At a safe distance; without getting close, physically or personally.
examples: She keeps her coworkers *at arm's length*.
The senator kept the lobbyists *at arm's length*.
He held the dirty sock *at arm's length*.

type: degree — limits a statement to the most favorable case
position: front or end — or right before the word it limits
modifies: a clause, an adjective, or a number
contrast: The opposite is *at worst*. *At the best of times* is a separate phrase: *He's grumpy at the best of times* (даже в хорошие дни).

senses.gloss: Even in the most favorable view; no better than.
examples: The plan is risky *at best*.
We'll break even this year, *at best*.
*At best*, the repairs will take a week.

modifies: verbs of shooting, seeing and watching

senses.gloss: From very near.
examples: The victim was shot *at close range*.
We watched the whales *at close range*.
Seen *at close range*, the moon rock looked like ordinary gravel.

type: viewpoint — a first impression that may change
contrast: More bookish than *at first glance*; nothing to do with blushing.

senses.gloss: When first considered; on first impression.
examples: *At first blush*, the offer seems generous.
The idea sounds crazy *at first blush*.
*At first blush*, the two cases look alike.

type: viewpoint — a first impression that may change
contrast: For a first impression Americans usually say *at first glance*; *at first sight* is mostly *love at first sight*.

senses.gloss: When first seen, before looking closely.
examples: *At first glance*, the problem looks simple.
The two paintings look identical *at first glance*.
*At first glance*, it's an ordinary house.

ru: с первого взгляда; на первый взгляд
position: end — or front for the first-impression sense
modifies: verbs of loving and recognizing; a whole clause
contrast: Its most common use is *love at first sight* (любовь с первого взгляда). For a first impression *at first glance* is more usual.

senses.gloss: The moment someone or something is first seen.
examples: It was love *at first sight*.
He recognized her *at first sight*.

senses.gloss: On first impression, before looking closely.
examples: *At first sight*, the job looked easy.
The theory seems convincing *at first sight*.

type: viewpoint — what someone really is inside
position: mid or end — after *be*, or at the end
modifies: *be* with a noun or adjective; a whole clause
contrast: Different from *by heart* (наизусть). *Have someone's interests at heart* means to care about them.

senses.gloss: In one's real nature; basically.
examples: He's a kind man *at heart*.
She's still a small-town girl *at heart*.
*At heart*, the book is a love story.

contrast: Americans often drop *at* after *stay* and *be*: *stay home*, *Is Mom home?* After a verb of motion there is never *at*: *go home*, not *go at home*. *Feel at home* and *Make yourself at home* mean comfortable, as in one's own house (как дома).

senses.gloss: In one's own house.
examples: I left my phone *at home*.
She works *at home* on Fridays.
Will you be *at home* tonight?

senses.gloss: In one's own country, not abroad.
examples: The president is popular abroad but not *at home*.
The company sells more overseas than *at home*.

type: manner — free and not caught; also, after a noun, as a whole
position: after its word — after *be* or *remain*, or after a noun (*society at large*)
contrast: Not *largely* (в основном). In American politics a *member at large* represents a whole city or state, not one district.

senses.gloss: Free and not yet caught, of a criminal or animal.
examples: The escaped prisoner is still *at large*.
Police warned that the gunman remained *at large*.

senses.gloss: As a whole; in general, after a noun.
examples: The decision will affect society *at large*.
The public *at large* knows little about the issue.

contrast: *At last* follows a long wait and shows relief. For the final item in a list use *finally* or *lastly*: *Finally, add the salt*, not *At last, add the salt*.

senses.gloss: After a long time or much waiting.
examples: *At last*, the rain stopped.
We're home *at last*!
She had found a job she loved *at last*.

ru: не меньше; по крайней мере, хотя бы
position: before its word — before a number; front or mid as a comment
modifies: numbers and amounts; a whole clause
contrast: As a comment it often points to something good in a bad situation: *At least nobody was hurt* (хорошо хоть). *At the least* is a rarer variant.

senses.gloss: Not less than; possibly more.
examples: The trip takes *at least* three hours.
She must be *at least* sixty.
Drink *at least* eight glasses of water a day.

senses.gloss: Anyway; used to point out something good, or to limit what was said.
examples: The food was bad, but *at least* it was cheap.
Call her, or *at least* send a text.

position: end — or front in the *finally* sense
modifies: verbs of speaking, writing and discussing
contrast: The *finally* sense is literary; in everyday American English *at length* almost always means *for a long time, in detail*.

senses.gloss: For a long time and in great detail.
examples: The professor spoke *at length* about the causes of the war.
We discussed the plan *at length*.

senses.gloss: After a long time; finally.
examples: *At length*, the door opened.
*At length* he agreed to see a doctor.

contrast: A stronger, more emotional *at last*.

senses.gloss: Finally, after a very long wait.
examples: *At long last*, the bridge is open.
The package arrived *at long last*.
*At long last*, she got the recognition she deserved.

position: before its word — before a number; or end (*twenty minutes at most*)
modifies: numbers and amounts; a whole clause
contrast: *At the most* is a common spoken variant. Not *mostly* (в основном).

senses.gloss: Not more than; possibly less.
examples: The walk takes twenty minutes *at most*.
There were *at most* a dozen people in the audience.
*At most*, you'll pay a small fine.

contrast: *At once* (немедленно) is more formal than *right away*. *All at once* usually means *suddenly*. For a single occasion say *once*: *I went there once*.

senses.gloss: Immediately; without delay.
examples: Come here *at once*!
The doctor saw him *at once*.
I knew *at once* that something was wrong.

senses.gloss: At the same time; together.
examples: Don't all talk *at once*.
I can't do three things *at once*.

position: any position — front, mid after *be*, or end
contrast: *At one time* meaning *formerly* (когда-то) is not *at once* (сразу).

senses.gloss: In the past; formerly.
examples: *At one time*, this town had three movie theaters.
She was *at one time* the best player on the team.

senses.gloss: Together; at the same time.
examples: The elevator holds only eight people *at one time*.
Don't take more than two pills *at one time*.

contrast: More formal than *at the moment* or *right now*. No article: *at present*, not *at the present*.

senses.gloss: Now; at this time.
examples: *At present*, there are no plans to close the school.
The position is not available *at present*.
We have about 200 employees *at present*.

contrast: The one-word adverb is *randomly*. In slang the adjective *random* also means strange or unexpected.

senses.gloss: Without a plan, choice or pattern.
examples: The winners will be chosen *at random*.
He opened the book *at random* and began to read.
The attacker seemed to pick victims *at random*.

type: manner — describes what may be won or lost
position: after its word — after *be*, or after a noun (*the money at stake*)
modifies: *be*; nouns for what can be lost
contrast: Spelled *stake*, not *steak*. Close to *at risk*, but *at risk* usually means danger to people or things.

senses.gloss: At risk; able to be lost or won, depending on the outcome.
examples: Thousands of jobs are *at stake*.
With so much money *at stake*, nobody wants to make a mistake.
Her reputation was *at stake*.

position: front or end — front with a comma in the linking sense
contrast: In the linking sense it introduces a contrasting fact, not a time — like Russian *вместе с тем*.

senses.gloss: Together; simultaneously.
examples: We both started talking *at the same time*.
You can't text and drive *at the same time*.

senses.gloss: However; on the other hand.
senses.ru: в то же время, вместе с тем
examples: I want to help him. *At the same time*, I don't want to be used.
The job pays well; *at the same time*, the hours are terrible.

contrast: Not *at a time* (за раз) or *at one time* (когда-то).

senses.gloss: Sometimes; occasionally.
examples: *At times*, I wonder if I made the right choice.
The road can be dangerous *at times*.
He can be difficult *at times*.

contrast: In US law, *at-will employment* means either side can end the job at any time without giving a reason.

senses.gloss: Whenever or however one wants.
examples: The cat comes and goes *at will*.
Users can change the settings *at will*.
He seemed able to cry *at will*.

type: degree — limits a statement to the least favorable case
contrast: The opposite of *at best*, and often paired with it: *careless at best, dishonest at worst*.

senses.gloss: In the worst possible case.
examples: *At worst*, we'll have to start over.
The side effects are mild *at worst*.
His remarks were careless at best and dishonest *at worst*.

modifies: verbs of moving, talking and writing
contrast: Americans say *back and forth*; *backwards and forwards* is more British. Also a noun: *the back-and-forth of the negotiations*.

senses.gloss: From one place or side to another and back again, repeatedly.
examples: He paced *back and forth* across the room.
We emailed *back and forth* for weeks.
The kids ran *back and forth* between the two houses.

contrast: Not *long before* (задолго до): *Before long he left* (вскоре ушёл) vs *long before he left* (задолго до его ухода).

senses.gloss: Soon; after a short time.
examples: *Before long*, the whole town knew.
You'll be walking again *before long*.
It got dark *before long*, and we headed back.

senses.gloss: Unfairly, especially by attacking someone's weak point.
examples: Bringing up his divorce in the debate was hitting *below the belt*.
That comment was a little *below the belt*.
The campaign ads went *below the belt*.

position: front — usually before the last item
modifies: a whole clause, or the last item of a list
contrast: The opposite is *worst of all*.

senses.gloss: Most pleasing of all the things mentioned.
examples: The hotel is clean, cheap and, *best of all*, right on the beach.
*Best of all*, the tickets are free.
I like all her books, but I like this one *best of all*.

term: beyond a shadow of a doubt
ipa: bɪˌjɑːnd ə ˌʃædoʊ əv ə ˈdaʊt
respell: bi-yahnd uh shad-oh uhv uh DOWT
modifies: verbs of knowing and proving; a whole clause
contrast: The legal standard is *beyond a reasonable doubt*, which is weaker.

senses.gloss: With complete certainty.
examples: The DNA proved *beyond a shadow of a doubt* that he was there.
I knew *beyond a shadow of a doubt* that she was the one.
*Beyond a shadow of a doubt*, this is his best album.

position: end — usually after *be* or a verb of proving
contrast: Formal. Speech prefers *without a doubt*; *no doubt* often means only *probably*.

senses.gloss: So certainly that no one can question it.
examples: His honesty is *beyond doubt*.
The tests proved *beyond doubt* that the water was safe.
It is now *beyond doubt* that the painting is a fake.

position: after its word — after an adjective or verb

senses.gloss: Extremely; more than can be measured.
examples: She was grateful *beyond measure*.
His music has enriched our lives *beyond measure*.
The war caused suffering *beyond measure*.

senses.gloss: Gradually; a little at a time.
examples: *Bit by bit*, the town was rebuilt.
He paid off the debt *bit by bit*.
She's getting her strength back *bit by bit*.

senses.gloss: In general, ignoring details and exceptions.
examples: *Broadly speaking*, prices in the city are higher.
*Broadly speaking*, there are two kinds of learners.
The results were, *broadly speaking*, positive.

ru: но ведь, но с другой стороны
type: linking — balances or explains what was said
contrast: Not a time sequence like *and then* (потом): *but then* adds a fact that explains or balances the last one. *But then again* is the same, more tentative.

senses.gloss: On the other hand; but it should be remembered that.
senses.ru: но ведь, но с другой стороны
examples: The food was expensive, *but then* it was the best in town.
He's not very fit — *but then* he's almost eighty.
I might go. *But then* again, I might not.

ru: далеко не; безусловно, с большим отрывом
type: degree — strengthens a negative or a superlative
modifies: a negative clause or a superlative
contrast: *A long shot* alone is a noun: an attempt unlikely to succeed. *Not by a long shot* is informal American for *not at all*.

senses.gloss: At all, with *not*; used to make a negative stronger.
examples: The fight isn't over — not *by a long shot*.
She isn't the best player on the team *by a long shot*.

senses.gloss: By a large amount, with a superlative; clearly.
examples: It was the hardest exam of the year *by a long shot*.
He was the strongest candidate *by a long shot*.

position: front — often alone as a reply
contrast: Opposite of *by no means* (ни в коем случае, вовсе не), though the words look alike.

senses.gloss: Certainly; of course, used to give permission or encourage.
examples: 'Mind if I sit here?' '*By all means*.'
*By all means*, call me if you need anything.
If you want to try it, *by all means* go ahead.

modifies: a negative clause; verbs of getting and doing
contrast: *Not by any means* equals *by no means*. *By any means necessary* means doing whatever it takes.

senses.gloss: In any way; at all, with a negative.
examples: It's not a perfect solution *by any means*.
She isn't rich *by any means*.

senses.gloss: In whatever way is possible.
examples: They were determined to win *by any means* necessary.
Get the data *by any means* you can.

ru: в общем и целом, в основном
contrast: The words do not explain it: it has nothing to do with size.

senses.gloss: On the whole; generally speaking.
senses.ru: в общем и целом, в основном
examples: *By and large*, the reviews were positive.
The kids behaved well, *by and large*.
*By and large*, Americans tip about twenty percent.

position: mid or end — mid in polite questions (*Do you by chance…?*)
contrast: In a polite question it means *perhaps*: *Do you by chance know her?* (вы случайно не знаете её?) — Russian *случайно* works the same way.

senses.gloss: Without planning; accidentally.
examples: We met *by chance* at the airport.
I found the letter purely *by chance*.
Do you *by chance* have a pen?

senses.gloss: Because one wants to, not because one has to.
examples: She lives alone *by choice*.
Are you working late *by choice*?
He's a vegetarian *by choice*, not for health reasons.

contrast: The opposite of *by accident*. *Design* here means intention, not drawing or style.

senses.gloss: On purpose; as planned.
examples: The delay was no accident; it was *by design*.
The room is small *by design*, to keep it warm.
Whether *by design* or by accident, he missed the meeting.

position: before its word — or end (*the best by far*)
contrast: Mainly with superlatives: *by far the best*. With a comparative, *far better* or *much better* is more natural than *better by far*.

senses.gloss: By a great amount; clearly.
examples: This is *by far* the best pizza in town.
She was the fastest runner *by far*.
Walking is *by far* the cheapest option.

modifies: verbs of making, writing, washing and delivering
contrast: No article or possessive: *by hand*, not *by my hands*.

senses.gloss: Using the hands, not a machine.
examples: All the dresses are sewn *by hand*.
I washed the dishes *by hand*.
The labels were written *by hand*.

senses.gloss: Delivered in person, not by mail.
examples: The invitation was delivered *by hand*.
Please take these documents to the court *by hand*.

contrast: Not *at heart* (в душе).

senses.gloss: From memory.
examples: She knows the whole song *by heart*.
We had to learn the poem *by heart*.
I know his number *by heart*.

senses.gloss: By any means possible, fair or unfair.
examples: He was going to get that job *by hook or by crook*.
*By hook or by crook*, we'll finish on time.
She got tickets to the show *by hook or by crook*.

position: mid or end — mid after *be* (*She is by nature shy*)

senses.gloss: Because of one's basic character.
examples: He's a cautious person *by nature*.
Cats are curious *by nature*.
I am *by nature* an optimist.

ru: ни в коем случае, вовсе не
position: mid — after *be* or the first auxiliary; or front with inversion
contrast: At the front it triggers inversion: *By no means is the problem solved*. Do not confuse with *by all means* (конечно).

senses.gloss: Not at all; certainly not.
senses.ru: ни в коем случае, вовсе не
examples: The test was *by no means* easy.
This is *by no means* the first time it's happened.
*By no means* is the problem solved.

position: any position — front, mid after *should*, or end
modifies: a clause, usually with *should* or *ought to*

senses.gloss: If things were fair or correct.
examples: *By rights*, the house should have gone to her.
He should, *by rights*, be in jail.
*By rights* we ought to have won that game.

modifies: verbs of paying and renting; verbs of change

senses.gloss: Paid, rented or counted one day at a time.
examples: You can rent a bike *by the day*.
The workers are paid *by the day*.

senses.gloss: With each day that passes; steadily.
examples: The situation is getting worse *by the day*.
The baby is growing *by the day*.

contrast: Written *BTW* in texts. *On the way* (по пути) and *in the way* (мешать) are different phrases.

senses.gloss: Used to add something unrelated or to change the subject.
examples: *By the way*, your mom called.
What's your name, *by the way*?
I saw Mike yesterday — he says hi, *by the way*.

senses.gloss: By trying different ways and learning from mistakes.
examples: I learned to cook mostly *by trial and error*.
They found the right settings *by trial and error*.
Many early medicines were discovered *by trial and error*.

modifies: verbs of spreading, learning and finding
contrast: Also an adjective with hyphens: *word-of-mouth advertising* (сарафанное радио).

senses.gloss: By people telling each other, not through print or advertising.
examples: The restaurant became popular *by word of mouth*.
News of the layoffs spread *by word of mouth*.
Most of our customers find us *by word of mouth*.

position: before its word — before a number or amount
contrast: *Close* here ends in /s/, like *dose*, not /z/ like the verb *close*. Before a place it is a preposition: *close to the station* (недалеко от).

senses.gloss: Nearly; almost, before a number or amount.
examples: The trip took *close to* six hours.
*Close to* half the students failed.
He earns *close to* $200,000 a year.

modifies: verbs of seeing and looking; a whole clause
contrast: *Close* is /kloʊs/, as in *dose*. The noun is *close-up* (крупный план); *close up* with /z/ is the phrasal verb meaning *to shut*.

senses.gloss: From a very short distance.
examples: She looks older *close up*.
I've never seen a tiger *close up*.
*Close up*, you can see the cracks in the wall.

ru: что бы ни случилось, во что бы то ни стало

senses.gloss: Whatever happens; no matter what difficulties arise.
examples: I'll be there Saturday, *come hell or high water*.
*Come hell or high water*, we're finishing this project.
She was going to college *come hell or high water*.

contrast: American honors, from lowest to highest: *cum laude*, *magna cum laude*, *summa cum laude*. Also pronounced /kʌm ˈlɔːdi/.

senses.gloss: With academic honors, at the end of a degree.
examples: She graduated *cum laude* from Yale.
He finished *cum laude* in economics.
About a quarter of the class graduated *cum laude*.

ru: день за днём, изо дня в день
contrast: *Day after day* stresses tiring repetition; *day by day* stresses gradual change. *The day after tomorrow* (послезавтра) is unrelated.

senses.gloss: Every day for a long time, often tiresomely.
senses.ru: день за днём, изо дня в день
examples: He wore the same shirt *day after day*.
*Day after day*, she waited for a letter.
It rained *day after day*.

senses.gloss: Gradually, a little more each day.
examples: *Day by day*, he's getting stronger.
Her English improved *day by day*.

senses.gloss: One day at a time, without planning far ahead.
examples: Since the diagnosis, we take things *day by day*.
With no steady job, he's living *day by day*.
